summary: Cape Spencer Light on a Bay of Fundy headland near Saint John: first lit 1873, four towers in succession, the present fibreglass tower from 1983, run by the Coast Guard.

lens.note: original 1873 apparatus by E. Chanteloup of Montreal (LF)

structures.note: F. H. Carson of Saint John; replaced 1971-1983 skeletal tower
Coast Guard list gives 8.6 m; Rowlett gives about 12 m (40 ft)

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LF). High cliffs; LF advises extreme caution.

events.note: contract for the tower awarded to Clark and Stackhouse (LF)
square wooden tower, about 11 m (35 ft), with keeper's dwelling attached; cost $6,848
keeper given a hand fog horn
wooden fog-alarm building over concrete cistern; three-inch diaphone from the Canadian Fog Signal Company, Toronto, $7,250
alternating red and white light changed to group revolving white light (Marine 1910 report; LF gives 1909)
electric lighting plant installed at the station
new fog-alarm building and oil shed, $5,349 (LF gives 1915 and 1916)
octagonal concrete tower replaced the wooden tower
fog-alarm building burned to the ground on 29 November 1927; new building 1928
steel skeletal tower carried the light until 1983
present fibreglass tower entered service, replacing the skeletal tower

corrections.why: 1873 is the first (wooden) tower. The standing tower is the fibreglass tower of 1983 (LF; Rowlett). Record's 8.6 m height is the Coast Guard list figure for the present tower; Rowlett gives about 12 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: First light is 1873, from the wooden tower (LF; Rowlett 'station established 1873'). The 1983 date is the present fibreglass tower (LF; Rowlett). Both are right for different structures.

notes_for_editor: Moderate evidence. Four independent sources (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett, the Coast Guard list, and three Marine reports). Matched by OCR column position: the 1904 keeper-list line 'Blacklock, Fred. G | Cape Spencer' (p. 158) and the 1909 dwelling entry (scan p. 65; printed page unconfirmed, so cited by scan page). LighthouseFriends dates the J. E. Kanes dwelling to 1908; the 1909 report says it was erected that year, so the story gives both. The 1918 concrete tower rests on LighthouseFriends and Rowlett. A Marine 1919 New Brunswick block (identifier 1920v56i7p21_1511) lists 'Erection of 30 ft. concrete tower, 8 ft. lantern', but the OCR columns do not tie it to Cape Spencer, so it is not used. Height conflict: Coast Guard 8.6 m against Rowlett about 12 m (the station record's 8.6 m comes from Wikidata). Collins and McKee overlap in LighthouseFriends' list; no role is given for either. The Chronicling America search for 'Cape Spencer' with 'Bay of Fundy' returned no relevant page, so no newspaper is used. The Marine reports searched for ashore, stranded, wreck, gale and storm near Cape Spencer returned no wreck or rescue at this station. Do not mix with the Cape Spencer light in Alaska (a separate US station that appears in the 1915-16 Commissioner reports). No general-context passage is used. Keeper roster for Collins, McKee and Mitchell comes from LighthouseFriends only; they are named in public role with no personal detail. Fact-check 2026-10-28: all 45 evidence quotes were found on the first run. Story changes: fiscal years (Canada's Marine fiscal year ended 31 March from 1907; the 1904 keeper list is for the year ended 30 June 1904); the ownership sentence now cites Rowlett only, because the Coast Guard list names no owner; 'near the edge' removed (LighthouseFriends says only extreme caution in this area of high cliffs); metres first for height, road and site; the red-light range is given in miles as LighthouseFriends prints it. Image check: the 1904 keeper-list line (archive scan p.171, printed p.158) was viewed in the archive viewer; 'Blacklock, Fred. G' sits in the name column with 'Cape Spencer' in the station column, and the 1902, 1905 and 1907 lists print the same line. The 1909 dwelling entry is prose, not a table; its printed page is unconfirmed, so it is cited by scan page.
